subject: Observability PoC governance & data residency check-in
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@datadog.com>, partners@grafana.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability PoC governance & data residency check-in

Hi Maria / Grafana partners team —

Thanks again for walking through the proposed PoC scope yesterday. Before we lock dates I want to confirm two governance items that came up from Legal and Security:

1) Data residency for traces/logs during the PoC (we need to confirm whether Datadog SaaS will store any samples outside of US regions).
2) Temporary service accounts / API keys lifecycle and automated cleanup after the PoC ends.

I've attached a lightweight checklist that our security team expects for partners running a short PoC. Can you confirm: will Datadog be able to pin ingestion to us-east-1 for the trial, and can partner-level API keys be scoped and revoked automatically?

If yes, we'll proceed to schedule the first week of ingestion (we're targeting Oct 4). If any of this needs additional contract language, please flag and we'll escalate.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-datadog-poc-checklist.pdf, poc-networking-diagram.drawio

---

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@datadog.com>
To: aditya@redwood.com
Cc: partners@grafana.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability PoC governance & data residency check-in

Hi Aditya —

Appreciate the checklist. Quick answers:

- Data residency: for the PoC we can configure ingestion endpoints to route to us-east-1 and ensure no long-term retention in other regions. We will, however, keep short-lived processing replicas for ingestion scaling — those are ephemeral and covered under our SOC controls. I'll get the exact retention TTLs from our infra team and send them over by EOD tomorrow.

- API keys: we can issue scoped service tokens limited to traces and logs ingestion for the PoC timeframe. We have an automated revocation workflow; we can tie the token expiry to the PoC end date. We will also provide an endpoint to rotate or revoke the key immediately if requested.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood confirm the sample size and retention you want during the PoC? We want to make sure sampling rules match what you'll evaluate.
2) Networking/ingest: the diagram you attached references a private peering option. Is that required for Oct 4 or is a TLS endpoint sufficient for the first week?

I'll attach a short note from infra about region behavior when I have it.

Cheers,
Maria Lopez
Partner Solutions Engineer, Datadog
Datadog

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@datadog.com>, partners@grafana.com, aditya@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability PoC governance & data residency check-in

Thanks Maria —

Short answers from Redwood Security / Product:

- Sampling/retention: For the PoC we only need 7 days of full-resolution traces and 30 days of logs metadata (raw logs can be redacted and not stored beyond 7 days). We'll provide a sanitized dataset to seed the trial.

- Networking: For the first ingest week TLS endpoints are fine. Private peering is optional and can be added in Phase 2 if we see sustained traffic.

Action items:
- Maria: send TTL/region note + confirm token lifecycle by EOD Wed 9/22.
- Aditya: finalize PoC start date (we're still targeting Oct 4) and share PoC runbook link with Grafana partner team.
- Grace: schedule security sync to review checklist and revocation process (30 min).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

---

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@datadog.com>
To: aditya@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: partners@grafana.com
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability PoC governance & data residency check-in

Aditya / Laura —

Follow-up with the infra note as promised:
- Ingestion routing to us-east-1 is supported. Short-lived replicas may touch other regions for autoscaling (<4 hours) but no long-term storage occurs outside us-east-1.
- Default retention for traces is 7 days for standard PoCs; logs metadata retained 30 days. We can enable additional retention for metrics on request (billing note applies).
- Token lifecycle: we can issue scoped tokens that auto-expire on 2026-10-12 (PoC end) and provide an API to revoke immediately. We will also publish the revocation webhook so Redwood can trigger it from your runbook.

Attaching the infra note and a suggested minimal runbook snippets. Let me know if you'd like a brief onboarding call with our security infra lead before Oct 4.

Best,
Maria 
attachments: datadog-infra-region-note.pdf, datadog-revocation-webhook-example.txt
